ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Low-intensity pixels (dark grey/black) constitute approximately 85-90% of the fluke surface, providing high contrast against localized high-intensity pixel clusters (white scarring) and the surrounding water background.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Primary dark contiguous region across both lobes. Distinct high-contrast white linear streaks are concentrated on the right lobe, while circular white outlines (rosettes) are distributed sporadically in the lower-central sections of both lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: A shallow V-shaped central depression with an estimated pixel angle of 140 degrees and a depth of approximately 5% of the total fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular pixel-amplitude variations along the entire trailing edge, characterized by distinct peaks and valleys ranging from 2-10 pixels in depth.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Broadly convex curve extending from the median notch toward the distal tips, with a slight recurve at the terminal ends.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Spatial clusters of white circular pixel rings (approx. 8-10 visible) located in the mid-fluke region. High-intensity white clusters (live barnacles) are densely packed on the outer distal tips of both lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Significant density of unaligned white linear marks, including parallel vertical rake marks on the right lobe and intersecting diagonal scratches on the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A prominent, wide curvilinear light-colored scar is located on the inner-upper quadrant of the left lobe. Extensive rake marks are visible across the central and right portions of the fluke.
other_distinctive_markers: Presence of jagged, high-contrast barnacle colonization on the extreme outer points of the fluke lobes, significantly altering the expected smooth geometric contour at the tips.
